record_notes.DCP-LETT-2033: After January 20, 1857; XML lower bound January 21 with open upper bound December 31, 1882, so exact date and period eligibility remain held. All nine body blocks, full separate Darwin memorandum enclosure, notes and bibliography read. Missing Hooker note acknowledged; Daniell withdraws grant request after 2042 despite lower catalogue ID. Gray January 5 letter addressed to the Hookers is third-party material, not a separate Darwin prompt. Candolle useful compilation defended without claiming monocot-range priority; family versus genus range distinction. Madeira and NZ absences question continuous land. Enclosed methodological memorandum asks whether a general remark is corroborated in distant classes: Wight Cucurbitaceae and Hymenoptera genera comparison, acknowledged vagueness, possible Hooker/Bentham examples. Interlined American- beside Irish orchid may be Hooker, not Charles original. Both proposed endpoints 2033/2018 are Darwin outgoing and cannot form a conversational pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2042: January 20 with supplied 1857, all seven blocks and apparatus read. Missing Hooker note conveys William Hooker/Bentham objections; Darwin has advised Daniell not to apply for Royal Society aid and written Sharpey privately. Thursday meeting and Huxley glacier questions separate. P5 millet passes through fish, then stork, then is voided and germinates; editorial summary omits stork and cannot replace that experimental chain. Daniell Cameroons accessibility is reported, not evidence of completed expedition. Worker 2042/2022 proposal joins two Darwin outgoing letters and falsely describes the actual grant topic as species/crossing; reject.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2066: March 15, supplied 1857, nine blocks and all apparatus read. P1 forwards part of Gray February 16 letter 2053, earlier last-page consultation with Watson; P8 latest Watson response changes plan so latter half returns to Gray. Do not claim Hooker received full list. P2 recalls Darwin tree-sex request and British/NZ results, matching Gray question. Gray content demonstrably known by March 15; exact arrival and possible earlier Watson witness remain distinct. P3–6 respond to oral Club remarks about accidental transport versus continuous land, explicitly request positive botanical evidence and distinguish ignorance from creation/extinction assumptions; no surviving written Hooker prompt. P7 protean genera. Earliest global activation must be reconciled with later Watson/Gray packet, not inferred from this witness alone.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2067: Incomplete letter starts mid-sentence, editorial March 21, 1857. Five body blocks and complete notes/bibliography read. Requests Drège work/list within week for fortnight loan, explicitly not the Flora paper already known, to compare ranges of species in large/small genera. Do not equate with old May 1856 offer solely by author. Weed-garden experiment newly begun; August 1 survival count in apparatus is future. Hooker Indian-flora work and Himalayan thistle question refer missing current material/oral discussion, not identified incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2073: April 8, supplied 1857, ten blocks and all notes/bibliography read. Returns Drège because unusable for genus ranges; Thursday/Friday arrival only hoped. Requests Hooker scientific help only when worth time, not a command to present-day reviewer. Specific Fucus, Juncus, Polygala, Oxalis, British/NZ/Himalaya variation questions and introduced/native Sonchus abundance query are answered in 2074 P2–11. Book progress and planned Emma/Etty Hastings visit separate; ill she refers Etty in context. Reverse response evidence must cite botanical questions, not unrelated P9 book-progress sentence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2074: Hooker Saturday assigned April 11, 1857, all twelve blocks, separate Darwin note, footnotes and bibliography read. Family arrived Thursday, lodgings today; Etty pale/thin, hope not observed recovery. P2 welcomes philosophical questions. P3 endorses Harvey strongly, Don more cautiously; personally compared hundreds of Juncus from 8–10 localities Panjab to 9000-ft Sikkim on arrival day of Darwin letter, exact date not supplied. Polygala/Anagallis colours and Cardamine phases qualify relation to climate. P5–8 tentative identical/variable classifications, raw diag/ramme layout, Oxalis controversial and preferably avoided. P9 explicitly cannot answer Sonchus abundance, predicts introduced type will become commoner; P10 possible parallels not measured abundance. Additional notices promised. Separate Darwin chapter-organization note is undated, neither incoming Hooker voice nor established April 11 knowledge. Directly answers 2073 botanical questions and is acknowledged in 2075.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2075: April 12, supplied 1857, all twenty-seven blocks, footnotes, bibliography and original table/MathML markup read. P1–2 explicitly value Hooker last-note cases and place them under polymorphism. P3 begins new detailed argument/question about environmental effects and alpine hair/flowers; preserve as outgoing grounding/query outside strict reply scope. Weed patch 3 by 2 ft, 59 seedlings killed, slugs versus competition revision. P5 fractions are 72/94 undried and 62/94 dried sinking under ten days; seven plants averaged 67 days. P6–19 comparison is consecutive paragraph rows, not HTML table: undried/dried durations retained, ten species rows and Heloscadium seed qualification. P20 MathML 1/10 followed by redundant plain 1/10; P24 MathML 1/7, 18/94, 64/87, latter followed by duplicate plain 64/87. Do not read concatenated digits as integers or duplicate quantities. Preserve original a little above 1/7 (.140) tension rather than silently fixing arithmetic. 924 miles derives 28 days at assumed 33 miles/day, not observed sea voyage. Acacia drying is wager, Kew trial request prospective. Hardy endemics and aquatic varieties new queries. P25 separate Emma letter received; no guarantee whole response prompted by Hooker alone. Future Origin results in apparatus not contemporary knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2084: Wednesday assigned April 29, 1857 at Moor Park, ten blocks and complete apparatus read. Missing Hooker letter forwarded here. Reported hydropathy improvement is personal observation, not external efficacy proof. Hairy-alpine generalisation challenged; Darwin admits reliance on casual authorities and uncertain Meyen/Gay/Wimmer memory, asks Arctic comparison. Falconer knows no actual transplantation case; Darwin remembers Pyrenean plants losing hairs at Montpellier, later quoted printed source says Toulouse. Preserve discrepancy. Criticism of dismissal of weaker observers is qualified and linked to own evidentiary uncertainty. P10 30–40 young molluscs cling to dead duck foot and survive 15/24 hours out of water; no completed long-range dispersal demonstrated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2087: Saturday assigned May 2, 1857, eight blocks and apparatus read. Another missing Hooker note supplies Anthyllis counterexample, balancing believed hair loss at low levels; Darwin promises source evidence, not already verified full claim. Reflects on possible self-interest in defending compilers and willingness to reverse large-flower claim. Heath-like Cape foliage refers one or more species per moderately sized family, not all Cape plants; British heaths challenge climate-only account. Etty little overall Hastings benefit; possible Moor Park visit and Wednesday return prospective. P7 118 pond-mud seedlings before departure, later August 537 is future. Mud collecting suggested, not executed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2088: Sunday morning assigned May 3, 1857, seven blocks and complete apparatus read. Just received final Hooker destruction of woolly-alpine belief, returns material and asks whether cover note wanted back. Underlying manuscript statistics/list not transcribed as an admitted incoming source. Separate Asa Gray alpine list returned, not equivalent to whole Gray letter. Proposed Arctic publication and later 1862 paper cannot reconstruct missing contemporary prompt. Mrs Hooker assistance to Etty acknowledged. No forced pair to April 11 botanical observations.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2092: May 16, supplied month/year, five blocks and apparatus read. New question whether unusually developed organ relative to close species predicts variability; crossbill beak and Himantopus legs examples. Nepenthes is explicitly excluded as whole-genus abnormality, not positive example. Requests plant cases. Dryness versus altitude and De Candolle dwarf/hair explanation hypotheses, Senebier authority; conditional relation of dry endemic regions, not settled findings. Subsequent June 3 response requires its own source review. No preserved specific incoming antecedent identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2198: Three surviving questions, incomplete undated list assigned June 1857; exact-day hold. All body, dating notes and bibliography read. Bound with separate question list possibly October 20 visit; June inference from May 16/June 3 questions and July 5 chapter completion, not exact dispatch evidence. Marianne/Bonin and Greenland flora queries; Danish man probably Lange remains identification inference, not book receipt. Cnestis/Connaris ovary/albumen/calyx differences prompt within-species variability inquiry. No surviving answers or proof entire list transmitted on single day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2099: June 2, supplied 1857, thirteen blocks, notes and bibliography read. Missing Hooker medal letter concerns Royal versus Copley, Lindley versus Hancock/Prestwich. Darwin no longer on council; do not imply council vote. P2–3 promises Sharpey letter in day or two, P12–13 reports now written within later section, not automatic proof dispatched. Earlier private Sharpey letter publicly read unexpectedly. P5 cork self-corrected to work; concern undervaluing Hancock and confusing cleverness/contribution. P11 rereading corrects his misunderstanding of Hooker relative Huxley/Prestwich ranking; preserve self-correction, not only initial judgment. P8 just-started journey conflicts with May 29 diary noted in apparatus; no silent date repair. Later Lyell medal/Beaufort death remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2053: Additional Asa Gray February 16, 1857 source fully read: twenty-two blocks, annotations, notes and bibliography. Acknowledges Darwin January 1 and November 24. Schoolbook complete, Morrow N Japan collection studied and manuscript sent without publication certainty, Wright collection expected. Multiple shared/representative American/Japanese cases; Agassiz anecdote attributed. Qualified glacial inference allows older diffusion; range comparison future. P7 asks why Darwin predicted tree mono/dioecy. P8–15 European protean genera US comparisons qualified. Full P16 long list read; relative badness encoded one/two/three underlines and corresponding formatting, not just words/case. Salix/Populus inclusion explicitly because poorly known. P17–20 indigenous/introduced assessments combine confident observation and guesses; indigenous form also can be introduced. Separate Darwin annotations undated; return request on last sheet relates later Watson forwarding. Footnote Japanese/N American flora discussion mismatched to bibliography Gray 1859 tendril item, no silent authority substitution. Darwin March 15 forwarding and precise tree question establish knowledge, but latter half returned to Gray rather than transmitted to Hooker.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2018: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 10 with year supplied, eight blocks and full apparatus. P1 thanks tree counts, finds trees in 38 families and separated sexes in half, regards association likely while explanatory hypothesis remains uncertain. Tasmania report future; growing chapter length unrelated. P2 answers wife inquiry plus separate Mrs Hooker note. P3 answers Lyell anecdote but Darwin has not seen the review. P4 torpid molluscs after seven days immersion show as yet one revival among sinkers and one among floaters, not universal survival; egg experiment failed. P6 Francis suggested floating carcass, pigeon 30-day trial succeeded for seeds including tares; 999/1000 predation is hypothetical objection, not measured probability. P7 oral freshwater difficulty and P8 Harvey approach new requests. Direct scope P1 tree portion, P2 first sentence and P3, not experiments.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2022: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 24 with year supplied, six blocks and all notes/bibliography. Missing Hooker reference on Leguminosae, uncertainty on Campanulaceae and unknown Portlock letter remain missing. Proposed Harvey inquiry not yet sent/answered. Species-definition comparison distinguishes naturalists emphasis and invokes previously read Aquilegia example; no single preserved incoming source supports whole discussion. Supposes black seed lost, rather than verified custody outcome. About a dozen dung seeds now, distinct from November nine kinds. No forced pair to 2014 because general botanical subjects overlap.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2040: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. January 17, supplied 1857, two blocks and complete notes/bibliography. Friday January 16 Daniell/Bennett discussions after January 15 Club. Advice on possible grant and collector project, not award or expedition already executed. Daniell zeal/experience, Hooker reservations, Bennett qualified support and perceived mortality risk are attributed reports. Darwin will follow consultation; no preserved specific current Hooker communication. Later Niger locality criticism in apparatus is not already established January 17. Hooker year endorsement possibly retrospective; meeting corroborates supplied year.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
